lead: Reno plumbing deals with cold winters, high desert sun and earthquake rules. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Reno.
risk: frozen pipes and sprinkler lines, water heater wear and aging pipes in older homes
risk_short: frozen pipes, water heaters and old pipes
why: The Old Southwest and Midtown have homes from the 1920s to 1950s with galvanized supply lines and clay or cast-iron sewer laterals. Newer areas such as Somersett and Caughlin Ranch have plastic pipe.
Cold nights freeze sprinkler lines, outdoor faucets and pipes in exterior walls. Nevada is earthquake country, so water heaters need straps.
water: TMWA gets most of its water from the Truckee River, which flows out of Lake Tahoe, plus wells. The river water is relatively soft.
problems: Frozen sprinkler lines and hose bibs
tips: Blow out sprinkler lines before the first freeze.
Strap your water heater for earthquakes.
Scope old sewer lines before buying.
areas: PipeMend works in Downtown, Midtown, the Old Southwest, Northwest Reno, Somersett, Caughlin Ranch and every other Reno neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Reno Building and Safety Division, and contractors must be licensed by the Nevada State Contractors Board.

faq.q: Where does Reno's water come from?
faq.a: Mostly from the Truckee River, which flows out of Lake Tahoe, with wells as backup. TMWA treats and delivers it. The water is relatively soft.
